idea: When to replace old plumbing pipes
title: Signs It Is Time to Replace Your Home's Water Pipes
description: Plumbing supply pipes do not last forever. Galvanized steel lines, common in homes built before the 1960s, corrode from the inside out, restricting water volume and degrading water quality over time. Even copper piping can develop pinhole leaks or exterior oxidation when soil or water chemistry wears down the metal walls. Key indicators that your piping system needs replacement include persistent low water pressure, discolored or metallic-tasting water, frequent joint leaks, or visible flaking rust on exposed basement lines. Replacing aging water lines prevents costly structural water damage and ensures clean, reliable water flow throughout your home. Consult a licensed plumber for a thorough visual and pressure inspection.
image_prompt: A detailed, professional macro photograph shot in vertical 9:16 format showing an exposed, old 3/4-inch galvanized iron water supply pipe mounted along wooden basement ceiling joists. The pipe fitting features heavy corrosion, deep reddish-brown rust scaling, and crusty mineral oxidation around a threaded elbow connection. The textured metal surface shows realistic age and degradation. The pipe is properly supported with a metal pipe strap screwed into clean timber framing. Lighting is soft and focused directly on the corroded connection, with natural shadow and selective depth of field obscuring the background joists. Photorealistic interior shot, authentic residential mechanical layout, clean photography, no text, no logos, no floating parts.
